title: 一杯美式咖啡  (Coffee With a Label Insider)

segments.t: At a cafe, Xingzi meets an agent from Yuanye to find out why singer Xin Huimei cannot perform on Twelve Singers. Listen to their conversation first.
咱们有日子没见了，你瘦了。
给你买了杯美式咖啡。
谢谢啊。
你要是没事，肯定不来找我。
还真有事，惠美到底有什么情况啊？
她现在跟公司闹得很僵。
登台演出的机会一律不许接。
演出雪藏？
对，公司只给她接综艺节目的通告。
你也知道，惠美就是个纯歌手。
那我们的节目她来不了了？
怎么了？怪事来了！
Let's unpack what they say. The agent greets Xingzi warmly as he sits down at her table.
咱们有日子没见了，你瘦了。

'We have not seen each other in ages, and you lost weight.' Saying "you rizi mei jian le", literally 'have some days not met', is a warm colloquial greeting, and "ni shou le" is a friendly compliment in Mandarin.
给你买了杯美式咖啡。
'I bought you a cup of black coffee.' In many cafes, "meishi kafei", literally 'American-style coffee', is how you order an espresso with hot water, counted with "bei", 'cup'.
谢谢啊。
'Thanks.' Adding relaxed "a" onto "xiexie" makes a thank-you between old industry friends sound breezy rather than stiff.
你要是没事，肯定不来找我。
'If you did not need something, you definitely would not come looking for me.' Casual "yaoshi" means 'if', paired with "meishi", 'have nothing going on', and "kending", 'definitely'.
还真有事，惠美到底有什么情况啊？
'I really do have something to ask, what on earth is going on with Huimei?' Slipping "daodi" into a question adds urgency—'what on earth' or 'at bottom'—when you want the real story.
她现在跟公司闹得很僵。
'Things are very tense between her and the company right now.' Literally, "nao de hen jiang" says they have quarreled until things turned 'stiff', a vivid image for a deadlocked dispute.
登台演出的机会一律不许接。

'She is not allowed to take any stage performance opportunities at all.' Combining "dengtai", 'step onstage', with "yanchu", 'perform', names live gigs, while "yilv buxu" means 'without exception not permitted'.
演出雪藏？
'Her performances are frozen?' Showbiz Mandarin uses "xuecang", literally 'hide in the snow', when a label shelves an artist and blocks public appearances.
对，公司只给她接综艺节目的通告。
'Right, the company only takes variety-show bookings for her.' In entertainment circles "tonggao" means a scheduled media or show booking, and "zongyi jiemu" is a variety show.
你也知道，惠美就是个纯歌手。
'As you know, Huimei is purely a singer.' Placing "chun", 'pure', directly in front of "geshou", 'singer', describes an artist who only sings and avoids chatty variety appearances.
那我们的节目她来不了了？
'Then she cannot come on our show anymore?' Putting "women de jiemu", 'our show', sets the topic first before "ta lai buliao le", 'she cannot come anymore'.
怎么了？怪事来了！

'What is this? Something strange just came up!' Short "guaishi", built from "guai", 'strange', and "shi", 'matter', reacts to a sudden twist arriving on his phone. Now let's hear the whole conversation once more.
咱们有日子没见了，你瘦了。
给你买了杯美式咖啡。
谢谢啊。
你要是没事，肯定不来找我。
还真有事，惠美到底有什么情况啊？
她现在跟公司闹得很僵。
登台演出的机会一律不许接。
演出雪藏？
对，公司只给她接综艺节目的通告。
你也知道，惠美就是个纯歌手。
那我们的节目她来不了了？
怎么了？怪事来了！

Just as the agent explains that Yuanye froze Xin Huimei's singing gigs while leaving variety bookings open, a surprise message arrives. You learned cafe talk with "meishi kafei", urgent questions with "daodi", and industry slang like "xuecang". See you next time!
回头见！
